components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Raised fill, 1px line, ink label. Every button that is not the one primary.

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Recessed ground track; mono options in ink-2; the selected cell is raised with a 2px signal bar on its bottom edge. Speed, chart metrics, dock tabs.

components.name: Panel with Headline
components.description: A column panel: one tone up from ground, 1px line, 6px radius. Its headline is a condensed label in ink-2, an optional mono count, then a rule to the panel edge.

components.name: What-If Row
components.description: The signature control: fork glyph and the question. Rest is transparent, hover raised; armed wears amber-soft fill, a 2px amber inset bar, an amber glyph and a mono repeat count. The only control allowed amber.

components.description: Micro group head; label in Small with the value in mono signal; a 2px slider filled in signal up to the value, a 14x18 ink thumb that turns signal on hover.

narrative.overview:
What-If Lab is a lab console for running experiments. The stage is the experiment; around it sit instrument panels: what you can change, what you can measure, what happened. Graphite panels, condensed instrument labels and mono readouts make it feel like a simulator you operate, not a gallery you visit. It is a costume-free control room: no bezels, screws, scanlines, glow or terminal prompts. Every control is a standard web control.

The signature move is two channels. Every world runs on a channel. ● NO CHANGE (blue, round mark) is lit from the start. When a what-if forks the world, ◆ WHAT-IF (amber, diamond) lights up. The same mark appears on the stage tags, the chart legend, the readout column heads and the timeline. The fork moment shows in three places at once: the stage chip FORKED AT …, an amber marker on the chart with a diamond head, and an amber row pinned in the timeline.
keyCharacteristics: Cool graphite ground with panels one tone up; the stage is darker still (both themes).
Three voices: condensed uppercase names, Barlow explains, JetBrains Mono counts.
Signal teal is the only control colour; blue and amber are only ever the two worlds.
Depth is three tones (ground → panel → raised) and 1 px lines. No shadows.
One filled button per view. One viewport, no page scroll, on every working screen.

rules.name: The Two-Channel Rule
rules.body: No change is blue with a round mark; what-if is amber with a diamond. The same mark is used on stage tags, the chart legend, readout heads and the timeline, and the fork moment appears on the stage, the chart and the timeline at once.

rules.name: The Temperature Rule
rules.body: Cool is reality, warm is what might be. Blue and amber only ever mean the two worlds, always backed by a mark shape (● vs ◆), a dash pattern or a label. Gain green and loss coral are for signed deltas only.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal teal is the only control colour: the one filled button, the selected segment's bar, slider fill, variable values and the focus ring. Never data. The what-if row is the only control allowed to wear amber, because it is the control that splits the world.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Condensed uppercase (tracked) names things, Barlow mixed case explains, JetBrains Mono counts. Mixed case and mono are never tracked; mono is never used for words.

rules.name: The Three Tones Rule
rules.body: Depth is ground → panel → raised, each separated by a 1 px line. No shadows. Inset 2 px bars are allowed only as the armed what-if mark, the pinned fork row and the selected segment's signal bar.

rules.name: The One Viewport Rule
rules.body: Working screens fill exactly one viewport and never scroll the page; only named regions scroll internally with a 20 px fade.

rules.name: The Meaningful Dash Rule
rules.body: Lines are 1 px and solid; dashes are reserved for meaning: the what-if chart line, the split seam on the stage, an empty ad slot.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and duration from a token; canvas code uses STAGE and FONT.
Do use condensed uppercase for names, Barlow for explanations, mono for numbers.
Do mark the two worlds with colour and shape (●/◆), dash or label every time.
Do keep hit targets ≥ 44 px, text ≥ 4.5:1, a full keyboard path with the signal focus ring, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do animate only transform, opacity and colour with --ease-out at 150 / 250 ms.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows, gradients-as-depth, scanlines, bezels or other sci-fi costume.
Don't use signal for data, or blue/amber for controls (except the what-if row's amber).
Don't track mixed-case or mono text; don't use mono for words.
Don't nest boxes inside panels or put a kicker above a heading.
Don't use pure #fff on dark or #000 anywhere in chrome; don't use track colour for text.
Don't pull in an icon or UI library; don't use exclamation marks in chrome.
